title: Proxies and Load Balancing Quick Revision
summary: Quick revision notes on forward and reverse proxies, L4 vs L7 load balancing, balancing algorithms, health checks, sticky sessions, CDN edge caching and anycast, from mental model to a final cheat sheet.

chapters.title: Proxies and Load Balancers: The Mental Model
points: Forward proxy sits in front of clients and speaks for them to the internet: used for egress control, filtering, caching and hiding client IPs; the server sees the proxy's IP
Reverse proxy sits in front of servers and speaks for them: the client sees one public address and never learns the backend IPs; used for TLS termination, routing, caching and compression
Load balancer is a reverse proxy whose main job is spreading requests across a pool of backends so no single server is the bottleneck or single point of failure
Comparison row: forward proxy is configured by the client and protects or controls clients; reverse proxy is configured by the server owner and protects or scales servers
Mistake: calling any proxy a load balancer, or assuming a single load balancer is highly available: run it as an active-passive or active-active pair with a floating or virtual IP

chapters.title: L4 vs L7 Load Balancing
points: L4 balances on TCP/UDP connection data (src/dst IP and port) without reading the payload: very fast, protocol-agnostic, one client connection maps to one backend connection
L7 parses HTTP and can route on host, path, header, cookie or method, terminate TLS, rewrite headers, retry, and compress, at higher CPU cost
Comparison row: L4 cannot see URLs or cookies so no path routing or cookie stickiness; L7 can send /api to one pool and /static to another
Example: AWS NLB is L4 (static IP, millions of connections per second); ALB is L7 (host/path rules); nginx stream block is L4, nginx http block is L7

Mistake: putting an L7 balancer in front of long-lived non-HTTP traffic such as a database or raw TCP, or using L4 and expecting path-based routing; also an L7 balancer replaces the client IP, so read X-Forwarded-For (or use PROXY protocol) to get the real client IP

chapters.title: Balancing Algorithms, Health Checks and Sticky Sessions
points: Round robin cycles through backends in order and weighted round robin gives bigger servers more turns: best when requests cost about the same

Least connections sends to the backend with the fewest active connections: better for variable or long-lived requests; IP hash or consistent hash maps a client or key to a fixed backend and only remaps a small share when the pool changes

Active health checks probe each backend on an interval (for example GET /healthz expecting 200) and use thresholds such as 3 failures to mark unhealthy and 2 passes to restore; passive checks eject a backend after real request errors

Sticky sessions pin a client to one backend through a cookie (L7) or source-IP hash (L4): they break even balancing and lose the session if that backend dies, so prefer stateless servers with sessions in Redis or a JWT

Mistake: a health check that only tests the port or returns 200 while the database is down, or a deep check that hits the database from every balancer and takes the whole pool down; also forgetting connection draining (deregistration delay) on deploys so in-flight requests are cut

chapters.title: CDN Edge Caching and Anycast
points: A CDN is a set of edge servers near users that cache responses from your origin: a cache hit is served from the edge, a miss goes to the origin and is stored for later requests

Cache behavior is controlled by Cache-Control: max-age for browsers, s-maxage for shared caches such as CDNs, public vs private, no-store to forbid caching, and stale-while-revalidate to serve stale content while refreshing in the background

The cache key is normally host + path + query string; add Vary headers or cookies to the key only when needed, because every extra key part lowers the hit ratio; versioned file names (app.9f3a.js) allow a year-long max-age with immutable

Anycast announces the same IP prefix from many locations through BGP, so routers deliver each packet to the topologically nearest site: it gives low latency, automatic failover when a site withdraws its route, and absorbs DDoS traffic across sites, while geo-DNS instead returns different IPs based on the resolver's location

Mistakes: caching personalized or Set-Cookie responses publicly, forgetting to purge or invalidate after a deploy (use versioned URLs instead), and assuming anycast suits long TCP connections without care since a route change can move a flow to another site mid-connection

chapters.title: Everyday Commands and Config
points: nginx reverse proxy plus pool: upstream app { least_conn; server 10.0.0.1:8080 weight=3; server 10.0.0.2:8080 max_fails=3 fail_timeout=30s; } then location / { proxy_pass http://app; }

Forward the real client details with proxy_set_header Host $host; proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr; proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for; proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;

HAProxy backend: balance leastconn, option httpchk GET /healthz, server s1 10.0.0.1:8080 check inter 2s fall 3 rise 2, and cookie SRV insert indirect nocache with cookie s1 on the server line for stickiness

Inspect a CDN or proxy with curl -I https://site/asset: read Cache-Control, Age, X-Cache (HIT or MISS), Via and the CDN's cf-cache-status, and test an origin directly with curl --resolve site:443:ORIGIN_IP https://site/
Mistake: trusting a client-supplied X-Forwarded-For for access control or rate limiting; only trust the value appended by your own trusted proxy, and set the trusted proxy list explicitly

chapters.title: Proxy and Load Balancing Cheat Sheet
points: Forward proxy represents clients, reverse proxy represents servers, load balancer is a reverse proxy that spreads load across a pool
L4 means fast, connection-level and blind to HTTP; L7 means content-aware routing, TLS termination and header rewriting
Algorithm picks: round robin for uniform requests, least connections for uneven or long requests, consistent hash for cache or affinity needs
Health checks: probe a real /healthz, set fall/rise thresholds, and drain connections on deploy; keep sessions out of the server so stickiness is not needed
CDN: s-maxage plus versioned URLs plus a minimal cache key; anycast: one IP announced from many sites, nearest route wins, failover by route withdrawal
